title: Laredo Port Named in 21-Defendant Federal Indictment Against La Nueva Familia Michoacana Cartel
excerpt: A federal grand jury in Del Rio indicted 21 alleged members and associates of the La Nueva Familia Michoacana cartel, including an alleged attempt to export firearms through the Laredo Port of Entry, federal prosecutors announced Friday.
content:
A federal grand jury in Del Rio has indicted 21 alleged members and associates of the La Nueva Familia Michoacana cartel, including an alleged attempt to export firearms through the Laredo Port of Entry, according to the U.S. Department of Justice.

U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas announced the 14-count indictment on Friday, Nov. 20, at a Homeland Security Task Force press conference in San Antonio. The indictment, filed Nov. 18, charges the defendants with racketeering conspiracy, drug trafficking, firearms trafficking, alien smuggling, money laundering and providing material support to a designated foreign terrorist organization.

Prosecutors say the alleged leaders of the organization are brothers Johnny Hurtado Olascoaga, 53, known as “Pez” and “Don Gabino,” and Jose Alfredo Hurtado Olascoaga, 42, known as “Fresa” and “Chino.” The United States designated La Nueva Familia Michoacana as a Foreign Terrorist Organization on Feb. 20, 2025.

The Laredo connection runs through the investigation itself. Charles Kerby, acting deputy special agent in charge for Homeland Security Investigations in Laredo, described at the announcement how agents pieced the case together from drug seizures at a South Texas port of entry, separate gun seizures and an investigation into a 2021 fatal migrant smuggling crash. According to the indictment, one defendant attempted to export firearms through the Laredo Port of Entry on Sept. 30, 2021, and the firearms counts include .50-caliber rifles. Prosecutors also say cartel members discussed obtaining military-grade weapons, including rocket-propelled grenades.

Ten of the defendants, including the two brothers, face counts tied to a March 15, 2021, migrant smuggling crash near Del Rio in which a minor died. The indictment traces the alleged conspiracy to 2006 and cites seizures including about 2.06 kilograms of cocaine hidden in a vehicle engine at the Eagle Pass Port of Entry in September 2024, and more than 1,100 pounds of methamphetamine, 100 pounds of cocaine and more than 500 grams of fentanyl seized by federal agents in the Austin area, along with weapons stored at homes in Buda and Bastrop.

Five defendants are in federal custody. The other 16 are at large and are believed to be in Mexico. If convicted, the defendants face penalties ranging from 10 years to life in prison. The charges are allegations, and every defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

Update — November 21, 2026

The five defendants in federal custody are Jesus Daniel Alvarez, Alejandro Diaz Garcia, Rogelio Ponce Esquivel, Apolonio Benitez and Omar Sixto Benitez, according to Border Report, which reported the names after the Nov. 20 announcement. The indictment was filed Nov. 18 in the Del Rio Division of the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Texas as case DR:26-CR-03395. Border Report also reported that the March 15, 2021, migrant smuggling crash near Del Rio killed eight migrants. The other 16 defendants remain at large and are believed to be in Mexico.

Update sources: Border Report, Nov. 21, 2026; U.S. Department of Justice, Western District of Texas, Nov. 20, 2026.

Sources: U.S. Department of Justice, Western District of Texas, Nov. 20, 2026; Texas Public Radio, Nov. 21, 2026.
